meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, somewhere else, and pasted it in. That's a paste, not a confession.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a citation error, Hale, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Noted. What exactly are you putting on the table?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's what an outline is for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then he'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, Hale, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, nothing on file, and I want it in my inbox tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want those terms confirmed in writing, along with a direct answer as to whether Owen was spoken to before the zero was entered. I expect that email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, and she still wants the terms in writing tonight and an answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached with time to spare.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its late-night times and then answered her claim that he drafted elsewhere by asking for that draft with a date, because it gave her something checkable she could not explain away.
What cost ground: you never answered her early question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, so it stayed open and went into her email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: right after owning the zero, tell her plainly whether you spoke to Owen before entering it, before you turn the laptop around.
